subject: Where can I find sample code for a Bayesian break-point model?

messages.author: 4b63675507b4aa11
messages.subject: Where can I find sample code for a Bayesian break-point model?
parts:
I am trying to estimate a simple logit (event ~ time) model in which there are may be 3-4 break points in time. I was wondering whether INLA can be used to automatically identify these break points and estimate their slopes. Thanks.

Shige

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Where can I find sample code for a Bayesian break-point model?
parts:
On Sat, 2011-07-30 at 04:14 -0700, Shige Song wrote:
> I am trying to estimate a simple logit (event ~ time) model in which
> there are may be 3-4 break points in time. I was wondering whether
> INLA can be used to automatically identify these break points and
> estimate their slopes. Thanks.
>
> Shige

Hi

inla itself cannot estimate changepoint models. however, you can
condition on the changepoint(s) and let inla calculate the marginal
likelihood. the attached example is simple, its just iid normals with
one changepoint in the mean level. by just trying out `all'
changepoinits, you get the posterior marginal for the changpoint (under
a uniform prior for the changepoints).

[ I added some extra stuff in the code so it will run faster ]

this can be explored further, and I point you to the report (to appear
in Bayesian Analysis);

http://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/r-inla.org/papers/changepoint-revised.pdf

hope this helps.

H
